quiz.quiz_title: A Bottle of Dew Master Quiz

questions.question: Why did Rama Natha neglect his inherited land at the beginning of the story?

options.A: He wanted to travel across South East Asia.
options.B: He believed in a magic potion that could turn objects into gold.
options.C: His wife Madhumati asked him to sell the property.
options.D: He was afraid of working outdoors in winter.

questions.explanation: Rama Natha spent all his time and money chasing a mythical magic potion that could convert ordinary objects into gold, neglecting his vast fields.

questions.question: What condition did Sage Mahipati lay down for preparing the magic potion?

options.A: Rama Natha had to buy gold coins from the market.
options.B: Rama Natha had to plant banana trees and collect five litres of morning dew with his own hands.
options.C: Madhumati had to chant magic spells for six years.
options.D: Rama Natha had to donate his land to the village temple.

questions.explanation: Sage Mahipati required Rama Natha to personally clear his fields, plant banana trees, and collect 5 litres of winter morning dew from their leaves.

questions.question: While Rama Natha collected dew, his wife Madhumati harvested and sold the __________ at the market to earn gold coins.
questions.explanation: Madhumati gathered the harvested bananas from the massive plantation and sold them at the market for a good price.

questions.question: True or False: The morning dew water turned the copper vessel into gold when Sage Mahipati chanted over it.
questions.explanation: Nothing happened when dew was sprinkled on copper because there was no magic potion; real wealth was created by selling the fruit.

questions.question: What primary moral lesson does Rama Natha learn at the end of the folk tale?

options.A: Magic potions require twelve years instead of six.
options.B: Dew collection is the best way to clean copper.
options.C: True wealth comes from hard work and persistent effort, not magical shortcuts.

questions.explanation: Sage Mahipati's strategy proved to Rama Natha that honest labor and productive agriculture create genuine gold.
